quantizationCaveat: NOT a same-bytes comparison. wllama reads GGUF Q4_K_M (unsloth/Qwen3.5-4B-GGUF) while Zero-TVM reads MLC q4f16_1, so this compares a runtime AND a quantization together — unlike the WebLLM pair in qwen35-4b.json, where both engines load byte-identical weight files.
protocol: same-session interleaved pair, greedy, cache_prompt=false so every run pays a full prefill; Zero-TVM 128-token target x 5 runs + warmup (q4f16_1, /local-weights, BENCH_QUERY="?model=qwen35"), wllama 120-token target x 3 runs + warmup (GGUF, /local-gguf), enable_thinking=false on both halves; medians

zeroTvm.driftNote: Downward drift inside the invocation (66.25 -> 57.66); the WebLLM-paired session the same day drifted the same way (65.62 -> 56.31) and gave 65.17. The median is load-bearing here.

notes: The first sweep of this model reported 0.00 tok/s / '+Infinity%' — the Qwen3.5 GGUF chat template enables thinking by default, so llama.cpp streamed every token as delta.reasoning_content and the page counted only delta.content. Fixed with chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false (matching the Zero-TVM half, which already runs the non-thinking template) plus a zero-token guard; these numbers are post-fix. bench/results.json is NOT written under BENCH_BASELINE=wllama. See BENCH.md 'Third baseline: llama.cpp via wllama (WebGPU)'.
